title: SEC weighs new rule requiring intra-conference transfers to sit out a season - CBS Sports
description: League officials are set to discuss a proposal aimed at curbing player movement between SEC schools
body:
League officials are set to discuss a proposal aimed at curbing player movement between SEC schools
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:36 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        There has been much discussion in recent years about players transferring within their own conference, and the SEC is set to examine a new policy of its own. According to Yahoo Sports, SEC presidents will meet to consider a new one-year ineligibility policy for intra-conference transfers.If an SEC athlete transfers to another team in the conference, they would be required to sit out for one season. The new policy actually leans on an old NCAA rule that required all undergraduate transfers to sit out a season unless they received a waiver.In previous years -- when there were two transfer portal windows -- players couldn't transfer within their own conference during the spring window. With the elimination of the spring portal window, the new policy would add an extra layer of deterrence for teams looking to poach players from one another within the league.
This is another step toward self-governance for the SEC as it explores options, with the future of the Protect College Sports Act in question. The bill recently passed the Senate, but it still has hurdles to clear before it can pass the House.In theory, this new SEC policy could be a double-edged sword for the league. On the one hand, teams would be less likely to target one another on the transfer market. On the other hand, the top transfers in the SEC may be more inclined to leave the conference altogether in favor of premier programs in other leagues.
As with any new transfer policy adopted in modern college athletics, it would almost certainly be tested in court.

It was remarkable how they allowed 14 unanswered points to the Los Angeles Rams in the final four minutes of the fourth quarter last week, and didn't convert a single third down. Seriously, Philly went 0-12 on third downs. Then, this week has been tough for the franchise.Saquon Barkley has an injured hamstring, his backup in Tank Bigsby was just placed on injured reserve, and the Eagles lost two starters on the offensive line. Right tackle Lane Johnson announced his retirement on Tuesday to focus on his mental health, and Cam Jurgens was traded to the Baltimore Ravens on Wednesday. I know Jurgens wasn't exactly impressive at left guard, but that's still two starters down on Jalen Hurts' offensive line as the team prepares to cross the pond. By the way, the Eagles are leaving a bit late for this trip, traveling on Friday. As for the Jaguars, Trevor Lawrence is throwing the ball with confidence, while the defense ranks second in takeaways and rushing, allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per game. They drop 30 points on the Cincinnati Bengals and then get run over by Deshaun Watson and the Browns. What the Steelers have working for them this week are two things: They are at home, where they are 2-0, and they have a rest advantage. The Indianapolis Colts just got back from London, while the Steelers had an extended break following their Thursday night loss to Cleveland. They covered against the second-worst offense in the NFL -- who didn't score at the end of the fourth quarter in the name of sportsmanship. Yuck! It's not fun to pile on Miami. We knew this was going to be a rebuilding year. The Dolphins are the only team in the NFL that has not held a lead this season, and they are averaging just 11.5 points per game. This is an opportunity for the Bengals to get off a two-game skid. It's true that Ja'Marr Chase is in concussion protocol and Tee Higgins missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday with groin and neck injuries, but Dohnte Meyers and Mitchell Tinsley really stepped up for Joe Burrow's dynamic duo on Sunday. Meyers caught seven passes for 82 yards! Also, it does appear Chase is making some progress, as he was a limited participant in practice on Thursday. Betting the Bengals on the road is usually lucrative, as Cincinnati is 11-4 ATS in road games started by Burrow since 2024.

I didn't think Bagent looked especially great in his first "start" of the season, but he relied on his powerful rushing attack, which generated 232 yards and two touchdowns. The Jets' offense was atrocious, recording just 157 total yards while going 0-7 on third downs. That forced New York's defense to be on the field for 89 plays. EIGHTY-NINE PLAYS. Chicago racked up 34 first downs compared to New York's seven. It was bad. As for the Browns, Deshaun Watson is playing the best ball of his Cleveland career. He's led game-winning drives in three straight games, and is finding success with his young playmakers. The Browns are actually the first team to have four players under 23-years-old that have racked up 150 scrimmage yards through four games in Denzel Boston (283 yards), Quinshon Judkins (273), Harold Fannin Jr (153) and KC Concepcion (153).  It's wild to say, but the Browns are the better team right now. The pick: Browns +2.5Projected score: Browns 17-13New York Giants at Washington Commanders (-3.5)Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox, Stream: Fubo, try for free)Jayden Daniels is back for Washington, which is maybe a controversial decision? Daniels is wearing a brace to protect himself, but he literally re-injured that elbow while wearing a brace when he tried to return to the field last year in his very first game back against the Vikings. If he re-injures it again, you have to wonder if he could further mess up that elbow. The weather in this NFC East matchup may be wet and windy, meaning the ground game will be important. Commanders running backs Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White and Jeremy McNichols are nursing injuries, while wide receivers Stefon Diggs and Terry McLaurin missed practice on both Wednesday and Thursday. title: Joey Porter Jr. ruled out of Cowboys' Thursday night showdown with Buccaneers - CBS Sports
description: Porter was unable to play in his second game with Dallas after being traded from Pittsburgh
body:
Porter was unable to play in his second game with Dallas after being traded from Pittsburgh
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:29 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After a solid debut with the Cowboys, there was considerable anticipation regarding Joey Porter Jr.'s participation in Thursday night's game against the Buccaneers. Cowboys fans, however, will have to wait another week to see Porter again. He was inactive for Thursday's game due to illness. "It's disappointing (he's not playing tonight), but we'll have to overcome it," Cowboys owner/GM Jerry Jones said prior to kickoff. "We got our work cut out for us."  Porter reportedly arrived at AT&T Stadium hoping to play, but he was sent home after being labeled as "very sick." It was also reported that Porter has a bad virus and has been vomiting. 
Porter, who was traded from the Steelers just over a week ago, started and logged 24 snaps during the Cowboys' Week 3 win over the Texans. He was targeted one time and did not allow a reception. Last Sunday was Porter's first game of the season. He was inactive for each of Pittsburgh's first three games, citing a back injury. The Steelers traded Porter after he claimed he suffered a setback in his back following practice. Shortly after he touched down in Dallas, Porter acknowledged that his back felt better. Porter held out this summer, hoping to get a contract extension. He is still playing under his rookie contract. 
Without Porter, the Steelers' defense struggled during their Week 4 loss to the Browns. The Steelers are currently dealing with injuries to cornerbacks Jamel Dean (ankle) and Jalen Ramsey (wrist).

title: Guardians vs. White Sox score: Cleveland comes from behind to force decisive ALDS Game 5 - CBS Sports
description: The Guardians have taken both games in Chicago after trailing 2-0 in the best-of-five ALDS
body:
The Guardians have taken both games in Chicago after trailing 2-0 in the best-of-five ALDS
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:54 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Cleveland Guardians came from behind multiple times on the road in Game 4 of the ALDS on Thursday night to take down the Chicago White Sox, 9-5. With the win, the Guardians, after losing the first two games of the series at home, forced a fifth and deciding game back in Cleveland on Saturday night. The winner will move on to face the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALCS. The Guardians fell behind 2-0 early and 4-3 after five as the White Sox looked to clinch the series in front of their home crowd. But Cleveland responded in a big way, pushing six across in the sixth to flip that one-run deficit into a five-run advantage. It was too much to overcome for the White Sox, who haven't clinched a postseason series at home since the 1906 World Series. The White Sox are also 5-0 in potential road clinchers (excluding 2020, which weren't true road games as there were no fans) -- perhaps a good sign for Game 5. As for Game 4, here's how things went down. Back-and-forth action in the middle inningsThe White Sox had a 2-0 lead heading to the fifth inning and it sure looked like it would be a low-scoring night -- a common theme in this postseason where, entering Thursday night, teams that scored four-plus runs were 17-0. In the top of the fifth, though, Patrick Bailey hit a solo shot for the Guardians to cut the lead to 2-1. Then, José Ramírez crushed a two-run homer to greet White Sox reliever Jordan Hicks and flip the game to the Guardians' favor, 3-2.
The White Sox responded with a rally of their own. A leadoff walk and then a one-out walk set the table for Munetaka Murakami. He singled to left field to load the bases. Sam Antonacci was hit with a pitch to bring home one run and tie the game, 3-3. Brenton Doyle then hit a sacrifice fly to give the White Sox a 4-3 lead. Next, Kyle Teel drew a walk to reload the bases, but Guardians reliever Erik Sabrowski entered the game and struck Braden Montgomery out to end the threat. It looked like a huge strikeout at the time. Little did we know just how huge. Guardians blow things open in the sixthWith one out, Guardians left fielder Angel Martínez was hit with a pitch and then stole second. Travis Bazzana doubled him home and we were, as they say, off. Bailey would single home the go-ahead run. Then two walks followed to load the bases before Ramírez singled home another to make it 6-4 Guardians. Chase DeLauter singled to make it 7-4. The bases were still loaded. Jo Adell, the midseason acquisition who had been an RBI machine for the Guardians -- including a three-RBI triple in Game 3 -- came through with a two-RBI single. 
All of a sudden, it was a 9-4 Guardians lead. Cleveland coasted from there -- until the White Sox mounted a bit of a rally in the ninth. Miguel Vargas led off the frame with a home run, a blast that preceded a few more baserunners and prompted a pitching change that might have an impact on Game 5 (we'll get to that), but the Guardians escaped here. The Guardians' offense was among the worst in baseball in the regular season and quiet at home to start the series with just three runs in two games. They have now scored nine runs apiece in the last two games and even hit two home runs in Game 4, their first two of the postseason.Looking ahead to Game 5The series has featured plenty of creative use of traditional starters and relievers alike. It's possible Game 5 would have been more of a traditional starting pitcher game. 
But there are complications. Gavin Williams should have and likely would have gotten the nod for the Guardians. He was 14-8 with a 3.76 ERA and an AL-best 248 strikeouts in 184 ⅓ innings in the regular season. He started in Game 2 of this series, and though the White Sox eventually prevailed, he allowed two runs in five innings with 11 strikeouts. The second run he was charged with was actually left behind, as he gave up a single and then was removed from the game. The bullpen allowed the runner to score. 
The complication here is that Williams was summoned to finish Game 4. Guardians manager Stephen Vogt had already used six relievers before going to closer Cade Smith in the eighth. Smith threw two innings in Game 3. Once Smith gave up a home run to lead off the ninth, Vogt didn't want to take any chances and went to Williams, who threw 18 pitches to close things down. The Guardians' plans for Game 5 are now in question. Williams certainly can start, but may not be able to go as deep into the game. Parker Messick was burned as the starter in Game 4. Tanner Bibee is a traditional starter and hasn't started in the postseason. He came in relief in Game 4 and was bad, but only threw 15 pitches. Foster Griffin threw 53 pitches in Game 3. 
After the game, Williams said he is on board with whatever the coaching staff decides. "I'm good to go. It doesn't matter," Williams said (via WKYC). "Whatever they need me to do, I'll do it. If I got to start, I'll start. If I need to come out of the pen, I'll come out of the pen."On the White Sox's end, the guy would be Sean Burke, at least eventually. In Game 2, the White Sox started Anthony Kay and removed him after one-third of an inning for Sean Newcomb. Burke came in next and worked 5 ⅓ innings, giving up only one run on one hit while striking out six. He'll get the bulk of the outs in Game 5, as he hasn't pitched since Game 2. 
In the regular season, he was 11-7 with a 3.34 ERA and 185 strikeouts in 172 ⅓ innings.
So, to recap, it should've been a matchup between Williams and Burke, but things have been so mucked up the rest of the series that we can't be sure exactly what we're going to see. Maybe the answer is chaos and that's always fun to the outside observer.Guardians looking to join exclusive companyIn MLB playoff history, 10 teams have fallen behind two games to none in a best-of-five series and come back to win the series. The most recent came in 2017 when this Cleveland franchise had a 2-0 lead over the Yankees, only for the Yankees to come back and win. 
If we're looking for a team that fell down 2-0 at home and then came back to win two road games before closing things out at home in Game 5, we'd need to go back to 2015, when the Blue Jays lost two games at home to the Rangers, won two in Texas and then had that monster seventh inning in Game 5 with the famous Jose Bautista bat flip. In fact, that is the only time in this format that a team fell behind by losing two home games and went on to win the series. The Guardians will look to join those 2015 Blue Jays.

        This is our fifth week of running through the injuries and I'm not sure we've ever had quite so many significant question marks on Thursday afternoon. I always like to make the point that if you have guys that are real question marks, you need to do a thorough check of your lineups before the Thursday night game. While George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb, Dak Prescott, and Javonte Williams are all must-starts, Fantasy managers may have some very tough decisions when it comes to Bucky Irving and Emeka Egbuka vs. injured players that we like more than them. If it is a truly 50/50 question of whether that star will play, I always like to look at my backup play. In other words, if you have Ja'Marr Chase and Emeka Egbuka, who is the guy you would play if you sit Egbuka and roll the dice and Chase is ruled out? If the difference between Chase and Egbuka is greater than the difference between Egbuka and your backup plan, then wait it out.Ja'Marr Chase working his way through concussion protocol, Tee Higgins misses ThursdayWe may have this one backward. Because the Bengals said Higgins was day-to-day, we have him in our rankings and we have Chase out because we don't rank players in the concussion protocol. Chase's return to limited on Thursday is a positive sign, but no guarantee he'll complete all the steps needed to play by Saturday. We'll feel much better about Chase if he's a full go on Friday. As for Higgins, let's hope he at least gets in a limited session on Friday. Joe Burrow is a low-end starter as long as one of these guys start with a great matchup against the Dolphins. If both of the Bengals' starting wide receivers miss, then Dohnte Meyers and Mike Gesicki might both be must-start options at their respective positions.Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison both limitedWe are more optimistic about Addison than Jefferson as of Thursday afternoon, but there are a lot of moving parts here. Let's start with the easy one: If Jefferson plays, start him and maybe only him in the Vikings passing game. If Jefferson or Addison misses Week 5, then T.J. Hockenson is a must-start tight end. If Jefferson is out, then Addison is a borderline WR2. Watch closely on Friday.Lamar Jackson not ruled out, not practicingJackson suffered an ankle injury in Week 4 and as of Thursday afternoon, we aren't expecting him to start. Tyler Huntley is the backup and he really limits the upside of Zay Flowers and Mark Andrews. Huntley has averaged fewer than 160 passing yards per game in his 16 career starts. We're still starting Flowers as a WR2 if Huntley is under center. If Jackson gets in a limited session on Friday, we'll have more hope that he will play. He is a must-start if he's active.
Stefon Diggs, Terry McLaurin miss Wednesday and Thursday practiceMcLaurin missed Week 4 and we are not expecting him to play. Diggs was working on the side field, and we are currently ranking him as a low-end WR2. If both receivers were to miss Week 5, we would move Antonio Williams into the boom/bust WR3 range and Jayden Daniels would move down, but not out of the top 12 QBs. Make sure you have a backup plan if you are starting Diggs over one of the Buccaneers wide receivers.D'Andre Swift limited, Kyle Monangai not practicing ThursdaySwift missing a Wednesday practice and going limited on Thursday isn't all that unusual. We feel comfortable he'll play and rank him as a high-end RB2 despite his Week 4 benching for fumbling. Monangai is a much bigger story. Head Coach Ben Johnson indicated they are just resting Monangai after his big workload and aren't worried about his thumb. We will feel a lot better about that sentiment if he's back at practice on Friday. View Monangai as a borderline RB2 if he plays and Roschon Johnson as a low-end flex if Monangai is out.Malik Nabers limited on ThursdayNabers is moving in the right direction after missing Wednesday's practice with knee soreness. We project him to play and rank him as a WR2. Nabers was awesome last week against Arizona and should have success against a suspect Commanders secondary as well. If he is active, you should start him, but we would feel better about his upside if he got a full practice in on Friday.
Keenan Allen limited again on ThursdayAllen had a limited practice on Wednesday and Thursday and may be trending towards playing. He would be tanked as a WR3 if he's active on Sunday and could help your Fantasy team, but he hurts the value of Josh Downs and Tyler Warren if he's back. Warren is a guy we are starting either way, but Downs would fall from the top 20 to the high-end WR3 range if Allen is back.Rico Dowdle limited again on ThursdayWe don't want to play Dowdle, even if he's active this week, but he would lower Jaylen Warren from a must-start RB1 to a mid-range RB2 if he can play. Warren was the better back early in the season and has been spectacular without Dowdle. We would expect Warren to maintain a larger share of the workload than he had in the first two weeks.DJ Moore not seen at Thursday practiceWe aren't expecting Moore to play, which is why Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir were so popular on the waiver wire. I agree with adding them, but I am a little worried about starting them against a Rams defense that hasn't given up more than 50 yards to a receiver all season. I prefer Coleman to Shakir but both are in the flex area of the rankings. If Moore plays through his injury again, he will be ranked as an upside WR3.
Michael Pittman out for multiple weeksHere's something we can feel more confident in. With Pittman out, we like DK Metcalf as a WR2, Roman Wilson as a high-end WR3, and Germie Bernard as a boom/bust flex. Pittman's absence doesn't impact Rodgers' ranking because Pittman's presence hasn't really impacted their offense.Dallas Goedert limited againWe haven't heard anything that suggests Goedert will play, but back-to-back limited sessions are a good sign. We are expecting the team to be without DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley, so Goedert could have a huge role if he gets to 100% before Sunday. We would likely rank him as a low-end TE1 if he's cleared, because he carries some risk of reinjury or a snap-count role, and because the Eagles offense hasn't exactly looked functional. Goedert's return would hurt the value of Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, and Darius Cooper. Wicks was also added to the injury report, so make sure he's okay Friday if you are counting on him.

We are already five weeks into the 2026 NFL regular season. Can you believe it? This week, the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars face off in London, the San Francisco 49ers will play the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks in Seattle, and Josh Allen takes on Matthew Stafford on "Monday Night Football." There were 23 games decided by one score over the past two weeks, which is tied for the most in a two-week span in NFL history. A total of 18 games this season were decided by a game-winning score in the final four minutes or in overtime, which is tied for the second-most through Week 4. The NFL always delivers, and we are expecting more fireworks in Week 5. Which teams should you pick, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 6 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports ResearchPhiladelphia Eagles vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-7) (London)Dajani (Jaguars -7): Our London Jaguars fans must feel proud. The team they've supported for years returns to the United Kingdom as arguably the best team in the AFC, and they will take on a squad that looks like it's flailing. The Eagles blew a 10-point lead to the Los Angeles Rams in the final four minutes of the fourth quarter last Sunday, and went an incredible 0-12 on third downs. If that wasn't bad enough, franchise legend right tackle Lane Johnson decided to retire on Tuesday to focus on his mental health, and the team traded left guard Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens on Wednesday. I know Jurgens wasn't exactly Larry Allen, but that's just another starter gone on Jalen Hurts' offensive line. 
Then, there are the injuries for the Eagles. Running back Saquon Barkley left last week's game with a hamstring injury, and his replacement, Tank Bigsby, was also injured and placed on injured reserve. Star wideout DeVonta Smith missed last week with a hamstring issue as well. The vibes are not great in Philly right now. Even if Barkley plays, this Jaguars run defense has been fantastic. They allowed a grand total of 17 rushing yards to the Cincinnati Bengals' running backs last week and are tied for second in takeaways with eight.  …  Prediction: Jaguars 27, Eagles 18Dubin (Eagles +7): I don't exactly feel great about this prediction given the way the Eagles have looked so far this season, but I'm betting that they can at least keep the game relatively close against a Jaguars team that looks like one of the best in football. They did the same thing against the Rams last week, despite all the injury and availability issues Dajani described above. Jacksonville should be able to win, but I like the Eagles to cover.  … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Eagles 17 Chicago Bears (-3) at Green Bay PackersDajani (Packers +3): I can't believe I'm backing a team that I think has looked like one of the worst in the NFL up to this point. They couldn't even cover the spread against an undrafted backup quarterback making his first start. But sometimes that's the NFL! The Packers return home to host the rival Chicago Bears, who are trotting out Tyson Bagent at quarterback. I'm not sure Bagent can run this Bears offense as effectively as Case Keenum can. Plus, running backs D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai are banged up and missed practice on Wednesday. I'm going to kick myself if the Bears cover, but Green Bay is 6-1 SU and ATS in its last seven home games vs. Chicago. Something weird is going to happen!   …  Prediction: Packers 21, Bears 20
Dubin (Push): The Packers barely squeaked by a Buccaneers team playing its backup quarterback last week, and now get to go up against another backup quarterback here in Tyson Bagent. I think Bagent can lead a more competent offense than Jalon Daniels did, though, and the Bears should be able to run the ball against this Green Bay defense. Chicago's defense has played surprisingly well this year, but it's basically been all about success on third down. If the Packers can actually sustain some drives, they should be able to keep things relatively close.  … Prediction: Bears 23, Packers 20Indianapolis Colts at Pittsburgh Steelers (-2.5)Dajani (Steelers -2.5): The Indianapolis Colts just got back from London, while the Steelers had extended rest following their Thursday night loss to the Cleveland Browns. I think that could play a legitimate factor in this game. One thing that stood out to me from Indy's win over Washington was how questionable the defense looked. Athan Kaliakmanis came off the bench and threw for 186 yards, one touchdown and an interception in his first NFL action, while Treylon Burks burned Sauce Gardner for a 47-yard touchdown. The Colts rank second-worst in the NFL in total defense and eighth-worst in total offense. I don't have much faith in the Steelers as legitimate contenders, but they've owned the Colts in Pittsburgh. They are 17-2 all-time when Indy comes to visit. I expect a competitive game, but I understand why the Steelers are 2.5-point favorites.  …  Prediction: Steelers 24, Colts 17Dubin (Colts +2.5): The Steelers have looked good for exactly one of their three games so far this year, and that was in a game against a Bengals defense that now looks a lot friendlier than it did through the first two weeks of the season. The Colts also have a fairly friendly defense, but I frankly don't trust the Steelers as far as Aaron Rodgers or I can throw them, so I'm taking the Colts to win a low-ish scoring game on the back of Jonathan Taylor.  … Prediction: Colts 20, Steelers 16
San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5)Dajani (49ers +2.5): This could be the game of the week. Two NFC West rivals that fought for the No. 1 seed in the conference last year and ended up battling in the playoffs as well. The Seahawks defeated the lowly Los Angeles Chargers last week, 30-23, although they led 27-6 at one point. The 49ers, on the other hand, won a tough battle vs. the Denver Broncos, 24-14. He also has the highest EPA per dropback (0.53) through four games since Tom Brady in 2007! The 49ers are 4-0 SU and ATS in their last four road games vs. the Seahawks, and 12-2 SU and 11-2-1 ATS in their last 14 road divisional games. Give me the upset.   …  Prediction: 49ers 24, Seahawks 23Dubin (Seahawks -2.5): I think these look like the two best teams in the league so far this season, despite Seattle's weird loss to Washington and the let-up the defense showed in the second half against L.A. last week. The Atlanta offense has been totally reinvigorated over the last two weeks thanks to an unstoppable rushing attack and some timely passing by Michael Penix Jr., and if the Falcons can keep that going against Jesse Minter's defense, I don't see how the Tyler Huntley-led Ravens offense can keep up. … Prediction: Falcons 24, Ravens 17Buffalo Bills at Los Angeles Rams (-3) (MNF)Dajani (Bills +3): This is a fascinating matchup. The Bills, after all, were just upset by the New England Patriots and have turned the ball over seven times in the past two games, while the Rams needed to score 14 unanswered points in the final four minutes to beat the struggling Eagles. Have the Rams even looked good this year? They got crushed by the 49ers, took advantage of the Jaxson Dart-less New York Giants, lost to the Broncos and needed a wild comeback to beat the Eagles. The Rams have put up yards, but the Bills have put up points. They lead the NFL with 31.8 points per game, while the Rams are middle of the pack at 21.3 points per game. The Minnesota Vikings have scored more than them! Even if you think the Bills are overrated, they were perfect against the spread until last week. The Rams, on the other hand, are 2-2. Buffalo is 6-1 SU and ATS in its last seven games following a loss. I'm going to ride with Josh Allen and take the upset, and hope that Jim Leonhard can do just enough to keep Matthew Stafford at bay.  …  Prediction: Bills 30, Rams 27
Dubin (Rams -3): So far this season, the Rams have alternated between looking like the Rams team we expected and a much different version than that. That's in large part due to the various injury issues that have resulted in some inconsistencies on both sides of the ball. The pass defense has been largely excellent, though, and the possible return of Aaron Donald should help the run defense. I don't think Buffalo has anyone that can deal with the Puka Nacua-Davante Adams-Kyren Williams trio, so the Rams should put some points on the board here.  … Prediction: Rams 28, Bills 24Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) (TNF)Dajani (Cowboys -8.5): I found myself rooting for new Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels against the Green Bay Packers last Sunday, given his story. Undrafted to now replacing Baker Mayfield in the starting lineup! I actually nailed the final score of that game at 17-14, and proudly boasted Bucs +3.5. Daniels kept up with Jordan Love, throwing for 148 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions to go along with 55 yards rushing, but the Cowboys are a different animal. It's true their defense is very much a work in progress, but Dak Prescott's offense is averaging over 30 points per contest. It's going to be tough for the Bucs offense to keep pace with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens at home in primetime. The Buccaneers haven't even covered the spread this year, and I'm not sure that streak ends Thursday night.  …  Prediction: Cowboys 30, Buccaneers 20 Dubin (Cowboys -8.5): Dallas' offense is too much for Tampa — or anyone else — to handle. I suppose it's possible the Bucs could muscle and run their way to a win, but given how the offensive line has started the season, I don't see it happening in this one.   … Prediction: Cowboys 34, Buccaneers 17

title: Ranking all 32 NFL teams into tiers: 49ers among the elite; Dolphins sit at very bottom - CBS Sports
description: Plus, the Rams still sit among the NFL's best despite slow start, and two squads sit at the very bottom of the ba
body:
Plus, the Rams still sit among the NFL's best despite slow start, and two squads sit at the very bottom of the barrel
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:56 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        We're just about a quarter of the way through the NFL season, and we've learned quite a bit about every team in the league. There's plenty of time for teams to either continue as they've been or surprise us by reversing course. But we have enough information to start making educated guesses about who is good and who is not, and who is probably just average.That's what we're here to do today. We're sorting all 32 NFL teams into the following tiers: The dregs of the league, the teams that are probably not that good, the teams that are probably average, the teams that are probably pretty good and the teams that look like inner-circle contenders. Let's take a look. Note: Teams within each tier are listed in alphabetical order. Tier 5: The DregsMiami Dolphins, Tennessee TitansThese two teams are really, really bad. They're not the only 0-4 teams, but they're clearly the ones with the least amount of hope.Tier 4: Probably Not That GoodArizona Cardinals, Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, Houston Texans, Indianapolis Colts, Los Angeles Chargers, New Orleans Saints, New York Giants, New York Jets, Pittsburgh Steelers, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Washington CommandersThese teams range from 0-4 to 1-3 to 2-2 to even 3-1, but the underlying performance and/or schedule they've faced indicates that they're probably not going to be legitimate contenders. Some of them may make the playoffs, but they're not likely to make much noise, if any. 
Arizona scored an at-the-time surprising victory over the Chargers in Week 1, but it has since gone 0-3, including a loss to the Jameis Winston-led Giants last week. Cleveland is 3-1, but each victory has required a game-winning score in the final five minutes, and the Browns have only out-gained their opponents once. Green Bay's defense without Micah Parsons is eminently beatable, and its offensive line looks like a disaster. That's probably untenable unless Parsons drastically changes the Packers' defensive fortunes when he returns.Houston is 0-4, and its defense does not look as good as expected. The passing offense has been good when Nico Collins has been active, but the Texans can't run the ball at all. The Colts have scored back-to-back victories, but their offense has looked nothing like it did last year as Daniel Jones works his way back from injury and the defense remains too friendly for them to be considered a good team just yet. The Chargers are the NFL's most disappointing team, and the less said about them, the better.New Orleans can seemingly only move the ball in garbage time, and the Saints' defense has been unable to consistently generate stops. The Giants are 3-1, but their last two wins with Winston at the helm have gone against the Titans and Cardinals, so we're not exactly buying into them being all that good. The Jets looked much more competent offensively until this past week against the Bears, and they've given up 381 and 492 yards to their last two opponents.
Pittsburgh has really only looked good for one game so far. Tampa hasn't looked good or even acceptable at all this season, and is dealing with a backup quarterback situation for the next several weeks. The Bucs could already be out of the picture by the time Baker Mayfield gets back — even in the NFC South. And the Commanders' defense is once again just not good enough for them to be a real factor. Tier 3: Probably About AverageAtlanta Falcons, Carolina Panthers, Denver Broncos, Detroit Lions, Las Vegas Raiders, New England Patriots, Philadelphia EaglesThe Falcons have been surprisingly good defensively thanks to the league's most surprising pass rush, and the offense has looked really good the last two weeks since Michael Penix returned. The only remaining questions are how real that offensive improvement is and whether they can actually keep up that pass-rush productivity. Carolina looks pretty good behind a resurgent Bryce Young, but defensive injuries could undermine the Panthers until their top two cornerbacks return.Denver's offense has looked miserable so far, except in the second half against the Jaguars, and now the Broncos will be without key players like Patrick Surtain II and Pat Bryant for a while. Still, there is upside with Sean Payton and then Vance Joseph's defense. The Lions have an explosive offense and a decrepit defense. It's hard to know what to do with them because they simply can't get consistent stops, but most teams can't stop them, either. 
The Raiders' only loss is to the Chiefs, and by just three points... but their three wins are against the Dolphins, Chargers and Saints, so we don't necessarily know how good they are just yet. We're waiting to see a little bit more before moving them up. The Pats haven't exactly lit the world on fire just yet, but they did just beat the Bills and looked good doing it. The Eagles have looked just as annoying as ever in both their wins and their losses, and they're hemorrhaging offensive linemen and skill-position players. The roster still has a lot of talent on defense, though, so if they can get things into gear on that end, they still have a chance to take the NFC East.Tier 2: Probably Pretty GoodBaltimore Ravens, Chicago Bears, Cincinnati Bengals, Dallas Cowboys, Minnesota VikingsThe Ravens have looked incredible whenever Zay Flowers has been on the field. So long as Lamar Jackson's injury isn't long-term and doesn't hamper him when he returns, we feel pretty comfortable declaring them a good team. The same goes for the Bears, who have been able to run the ball on everyone except the Vikings and should get Caleb Williams back fairly soon. Their defense has also been surprisingly effective so far, even though much of that has been about their third-down performance.We need to monitor the injuries to Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor), but we know how good Cincinnati's offense can be when all the principals are healthy, and the defense has looked better than it did last year. The Dallas defense looks as bad as ever, but the Cowboys have scored at a rate that would rank the best in the NFL since 2000 (3.39 points per drive). When your offense is that good, you can overcome a bad defense — at least during the regular season. Minnesota is the inverse of Dallas. The defense is so good that it can overcome an offense that looks less than ordinary. 
Tier 1: The Inner Circle (For Now)Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Kansas City Chiefs, Los Angeles Rams, San Francisco 49ers, Seattle SeahawksBuffalo hit a snag in its game last week against the Patriots, but it has otherwise looked pretty excellent. While we need to keep an eye on Jim Leonhard's defense, the offense should bounce back compared to how it looked a week ago. Aside from the aforementioned second half against Denver, Jacksonville has looked like one of the league's elite teams. We're willing to consider that the exception to the rule and keep them in this group.Kansas City might need to find some help at wide receiver after injuries to Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton, but Kenneth Walker III has taken the offense to another level, and the defense under Steve Spagnuolo always rounds into playoff form eventually. The Rams have alternated looking ordinary (or worse) with looking much more like the team we expected coming into the season, but so long as they can make it through the season healthy, they have as high a two-way upside as any team in the NFL.San Francisco and Seattle have looked like the two best teams in the league so far. The Niners cannot be stopped offensively, and despite a blip against Washington, the Seahawks still have arguably the NFL's best defense when healthy (it's them or the Vikings). Both of those teams should be a major factor all year long.

body:
Dallas brings a historically efficient scoring attack into Thursday night against an 0-4 Tampa Bay squad turning to rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:25 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the Week 5 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Dallas Cowboys play host to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Dallas rebounded last week from its heartbreaking loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro the week before, storming back from a double-digit deficit to defeat the Houston Texans with a furious fourth-quarter rally. The Cowboys have arguably the NFL's best offense through the first four weeks of the season, and it could get a lift here with the potential return of guard Tyler Smith. But the Cowboys also have arguably the league's worst defense, and that unit is still dealing with various injuries even after trading for Joey Porter Jr.Tampa is coming off a dispiriting loss to the Green Bay Packers in the first game of the Jalon Daniels era. The Buccaneers have turned to Daniels in the wake of Baker Mayfield's thumb injury, and the offense sputtered in his first game under center, totaling just 275 yards while Daniels was intercepted twice. The Bucs are now 0-4 after that loss and already in danger of falling out of the playoff picture entirely just a month into the NFL season.Will Dallas get over .500 for the first time, or will Tampa capture its first win of the season? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.Where to watch Cowboys vs. Buccaneers liveDate: Thursday, Oct. 8 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ETLocation: AT&T Stadium (Arlington, Texas)Streaming: Amazon PrimeFollow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Cowboys -8.5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings SportsbookWhen the Buccaneers have the ballThe Bucs went fairly run-heavy against the Packers in Daniels' first start, with the undrafted rookie throwing 27 passes while the team totaled 31 rush attempts despite trailing for most of the afternoon. Daniels went 19 of 27 for just 148 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also rushing eight times for 55 yards. Six of those runs were scrambles, and he totaled 46 yards on those plays.
The Cowboys have faced mobile quarterbacks three times this year and given up a ton of rushing yards to them. Jaxson Dart ran 11 times for 54 yards, Jayden Daniels ran for 69 yards on seven carries in just one half and Lamar Jackson ran six times for 50 yards. Dallas does not have a strong pass rush to begin with (the Cowboys are 21st in pressure rate and 29th in sack rate), and the Cowboys have also allowed the highest scramble rate in the NFL while yielding 9.1 yards per scramble, according to Tru Media. Daniels, if he can maintain his composure when he does see pressure (and he was pressured on 42.9% of his dropbacks last week), should have opportunities to take off.Tampa's offensive line has surprisingly not played all that well this year. The Buccaneers check in 22nd in ESPN's pass-block win rate and 23rd in run-block win rate. The team's running backs (mostly Bucky Irving) have averaged just 1.07 yards before contact per attempt, indicating that the line isn't getting much push up front. And that's despite the fact that they've run into eight-man boxes at the second-lowest rate in football.
The Cowboys, of course, have gotten clocked on the ground, yielding 4.8 yards per carry to enemy backs. They check in 24th in yards before contact per attempt with 25th in yards after contact, per Tru Media. Irving should have room to run here if the Bucs can get their line in order.The questions for Tampa's attack center on the passing game, where it's unclear whether Daniels can lead a competent attack. The Cowboys have gotten lit up through the air so far this season. Porter should help on that front, and he can probably follow Emeka Egbuka around the formation here and force Daniels to work the passing game through his other targets, but the Dallas secondary outside of him is eminently burnable right now. Daniels didn't look like a player who could push the ball downfield with any degree of consistency against a subpar Green Bay defense, though, and there are still questions about whether he'll be able to do it even against this decrepit Cowboys unit.
When the Cowboys have the ballSo far this season, the Cowboys have an offense that is not just one of the best in the league but one of the best in recent memory. Consider this: Dallas has run the fewest drives of any team in the NFL (36), yet still ranks tied for second in points (122), just five behind the league leader (the Buffalo Bills at 127). That's because the Cowboys have been historically efficient, averaging 3.39 points per drive. According to Tru Media, that makes them the sixth-most efficient offense through four weeks since the 2000 season. (The full-season record for points per drive during that span was just 3.19 by the 2007 Patriots.) When Dak Prescott called this unit the Greatest Offense There Is during the preseason, it's possible that he was not lying.It's been Prescott himself doing the lion's share of the work, too, because the running game has yet to really get untracked. Javonte Williams has five rushing touchdowns, but he's averaged only 3.7 yards per carry and gained five-plus yards on his runs at the fifth-lowest rate among the 26 backs with at least 50 carries so far this season, per Tru Media. Rather than Williams getting consistent gains, it's just been Prescott methodically working the ball downfield with short and intermediate passes and then occasionally hitting defenses over the top with a shot to CeeDee Lamb or, more occasionally, George Pickens.
Tampa's defense has done an excellent job of stopping the run (opponents have averaged 3.2 yards per carry, the second-worst mark in the NFL), largely because that's what Todd Bowles tends to focus on. Those efforts have been successful, but the Bucs have been somewhat less successful against the pass, and they'll be shorthanded here thanks to the absence of Antoine Winfield Jr. They'll get Rueben Bain Jr. back to help the pass rush here; he hasn't been particularly effective so far, but Terence Steele has been friendly to opposing linemen who rush off the left side of the defensive line, so it's possible he could get going on Thursday night.The Bucs probably don't have anybody who can deal with Lamb, mostly because it seems like nobody can actually guard Lamb when he's healthy. It's easy to forget what he did the last time he was full strength and had Prescott for a full season: he was a First Team All-Pro and totaled 135 catches for 1,749 yards and 12 touchdowns. He leads the league in both receptions (37) and yards (498) so far this year. Pickens, by comparison, has yet to really make an impact, but that is probably coming soon enough given that defenses will presumably begin paying even more attention to Lamb. Pickens could have a significant size advantage against Tampa's corners on Thursday, and this could be the game where he gets loose.
PredictionDallas' offense is too much for Tampa — or anyone else — to handle. Perhaps if the Buccaneers still had Mayfield under center, they could win a shootout, but even the version of Mayfield that was out there to start this season would have made that pretty unlikely. I suppose it's possible the Bucs could muscle and run their way to a win, but given how the offensive line has started the season, I don't see it happening in this one.  Pick: Cowboys 34, Buccaneers 17

title: What's up with George Pickens? Numbers are down, but Cowboys WR is helping fuel CeeDee Lamb's historic season - CBS Sports

body:
Pickens may not be leading the box score, but his ability to draw coverage and create explosive plays has become a key ingredient in Dallas' offensive success
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:49 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys' (2-2) offense is once again humming through the first quarter of the 2026 season. Their Dak Prescott-led attack 30.5 points per game, and the most points per drive (3.39) in the league. Naturally, Prescott's numbers are elite: he ranks fifth in the league in EPA per dropback (0.24), fourth in completion percentage (70%), seventh in passing yards (1,065), tied for seventh in passing touchdowns (eight) and tied for seventh in passer rating (105.0). CeeDee Lamb has been on the receiving end of much of that production, leading the league in catches (37), receiving yards (498) and receiving first downs (28). Those 498 yards receiving are the most through the first four games of a season in Cowboys history. But what about George Pickens?Pickens has been a statistical casualty of Dallas' defensive struggles leading to the Cowboys having a league-low 36 drives this season. In 2026, playing alongside a healthy Lamb, Pickens has 225 yards receiving and no touchdowns on 18 catches through four weeks while averaging a career-low 12.5 yards per reception at the moment. However, Pickens is as valuable as ever if you ask the Cowboys.
"I think if you look at George last year, I don't know, you guys can look it up. I don't think he was putting up the insane numbers even till week four, five, six, whatever it was, because I think it's when CeeDee kind of went out, but George is learning the system as well. George easily could have had three catches for 180 yards in that game [on Sunday in the 34-30 win at the Houston Texans]," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "He really could have. He caught one with his eyes covered, and he opens people up all the time."  Pickens' role in the 2026 Cowboys offense, often, is that of the sacrificial lamb (pun intended) or field stretcher to open things up in the intermediate areas of the field. Pickens has run 45 go routes this season, the second-highest frequency in the league behind only DK Metcalf's 47 per TruMedia. Despite his high number of vertical routes deep down the field, Prescott maintains they're not making Pickens play decoy over and over again, even though that's what it may look like to the naked eye. "He's pulling two guys with him almost all the time, and I don't know if he's clearing guys out," Prescott said. "Those are all real routes, and if you want to leave one guy on them, I'm going to throw it to him. So that's just making the defense show us what they want to do. When we're sending them deep, as I said, if it's going to be one-on-one, I'm going to throw it down there [to Pickens]. If not, you've got to take another guy with him. and that gives us numbers advantage."
Prescott was true to his word on Sunday when Pickens finished with 75 yards receiving on two catches. His first catch of the day came deep down the left middle portion of the field for a 53-yard gain with 10:43 in the third quarter. The big play moved Dallas' offense from their own 36 to the Texans' 11. Nine plays later, Javonte Williams was in the end zone for one of his three rushing touchdowns that cut the Houston lead down to three, 23-20. 
When Dallas acquired Pickens in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers, many viewed him as temperamental after he appeared exasperated about not getting the football as the Steelers rotated through a revolving door of passers. His attitude has been anything but temperamental in Dallas. Some of that has to do with the knowledge that the Cowboys are trying to get him the football. Schottenheimer admitted he had a double move called for Pickens in which he was the No. 1 option on a play, but Prescott was hit in the pocket and couldn't get the throw downfield to him at that moment. What did Pickens do? He laughed it off. Only receiving three targets to Lamb's 21 on Sunday also didn't bother him because that happened to be Dallas' path to victory. "It'd be different if we weren't giving him the opportunities or trying to, and if defenses weren't just respecting him and taking him away," Prescott said. "So he's a guy that's smart, understands the game of football and he knows when the defenses are playing him that way, the opportunity it gives other guys. So he's a hell of a teammate, and I've said that. ... That [Pickens' attitude] shows a guy that's celebrating everybody else's success who obviously wants success, but as long as the team wins and he's doing his job, he's happy. It tells you how much of a magnetic personality he has, how much he loves playing football."

        A'ja Wilson has done it again. After yet another historic season, the Las Vegas Aces star was named the 2026 WNBA MVP, becoming the first five-time MVP in league history and the first player to win the award in three consecutive seasons. Though she has only just turned 30, Wilson can already stake her claim as the greatest player the WNBA has ever seen. For the sake of comparison, in the NBA, which has been around for five more decades than the WNBA, only Kareem Abdul-Jabbar (six), Bill Russell (five) and Michael Jordan (five) have won MVP five or more times. And only Russell, Wilt Chamberlain and Larry Bird have gone back-to-back-to-back. Wilson took 65 of the 74 first-place votes, finishing ahead of Minnesota Lynx rookie Olivia Miles and Indiana Fever teammates Kelsey Mitchell and Caitlin Clark. Miles received six first-place votes while Mitchell and Clark garnered two and one, respectively. PlayerFirst-place votesSecond-place votesThird-place votesFourth-place votesFifth-place votesTotal pointsA'ja Wilson, Aces659000713Olivia Miles, Lynx6401583442Kelsey Mitchell, Fever21225177287Caitlin Clark, Fever16201612212Breanna Stewart, Liberty07111425171Paige Bueckers, Wings003131670Angel Reese, Dream000309Rhyne Howard, Dream000136Shakira Austin, Mystics000113Gabby Williams, Valkyries000033Jackie Young, Aces000033Jessica Shepard, Wings000011This season, Wilson averaged 26.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.9 blocks on 52.7/40.4/86.4 shooting splits. Only a dozen made free throws prevented her from joining the vaunted 50/40/90 club; her 62.5% true shooting was 6.4% above the league average. Her 26.2 points per game were the second-highest single-season scoring average ever -- behind only her own 26.9 points in 2024 -- and gave her a third consecutive scoring title. The only other players in WNBA history to win at least three scoring titles in a row are Diana Taurasi (2008-11) and Cynthia Cooper (1997-99). 
Also a leading candidate for Defensive Player of the Year, which has not been announced, Wilson also led the league in blocks for the fifth consecutive season. The only other players in WNBA history to win at least five consecutive blocks titles are Brittney Griner (2013-18) and Margo Dydek (1998-2003).

Along the way this season, Wilson became the first player in league history with multiple 45-point games and the first player with five 40-point games, as well as the fastest player to 6,000 career points. She also broke her coach Becky Hammon's franchise scoring record with the Starzz/Silver Stars/Aces, and is now the only player with multiple 1,000-point seasons. Thanks in significant part to Wilson's brilliance on both ends of the floor, the Aces went 31-13 to earn the No. 3 seed in the playoffs. When she was on the floor, the Aces had a plus-13.1 net rating, and when she was off the floor, they had a minus-11 net rating -- a staggering plus-24.8 net rating differential. 
The Aces, who won their third title in four years last season, took down the Indiana Fever in three games in the first round of the WNBA playoffs. In the semifinals, they currently trail the Golden State Valkyries 2-0 with Game 3 scheduled for Friday night.

title: Multiple Power Four programs face College Sports Commission investigations over alleged NIL cap evasion - CBS Sports
description: Between five and 10 schools, including multiple College Football Playoff contenders, face scrutiny over third-par
body:
Between five and 10 schools, including multiple College Football Playoff contenders, face scrutiny over third-party arrangements designed to skirt spending limits
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Oct 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:39 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The College Sports Commission is investigating multiple Power Four programs for potential violations of college football's revenue-sharing and NIL rules, CBS Sports has learned.  Through public records requests, interviews and sources throughout college football, CBS Sports can report: The CSC is currently conducting longer-term investigations of between five to 10 Power Four programs.Among those programs are multiple College Football Playoff contenders. The CSC has been on campus at schools conducting interviews in person. The CSC has focused on "potential cap evasion and NIL-related violations between institutions, student-athletes and certain third-parties," per public records. These investigations of potential violations are not dissimilar from the NBA's investigation of the LA Clippers and Kawhi Leonard, where both struck deals with third parties to get around the salary cap. The CSC is looking into third-party deals that allow college football programs to skirt the rev share cap and rules. Multiple sources believe the CSC participation agreement, which would have given the CSC additional authority and provided a barrier against legal intervention from the states, is very unlikely to ever be adopted. No long-term investigation has been completed to this point. Some schools would like to see something done before the transfer portal window opens in January to serve as a warning to potential violators of the rules. In a memo sent to university presidents, chancellors, athletic directors and other campus officials on Aug. 20, the CSC stated:  "The DOI is actively conducting multiple, longer-term investigations into potential cap evasion and NIL-related violations by institutions, student-athletes, and certain third parties. The CSC encourages anyone with relevant information to contact the DOI. Input from athletic department staff on recruiting practices, agent conduct, and questionable business proposals helps the CSC apply the rules fairly by bringing potential violations to light."  
The investigations represent the most significant test yet of the CSC's ability to police college football's revenue-sharing system at a time in which roster costs have rocketed past the around $21.5 million rev share number dictated in the House settlement.  In conversations with 20-plus sources across college football, CBS Sports has learned that the CSC has been on campus at schools conducting interviews about active investigations regarding cap-evasion practices. There is no exact timeline on when those might be completed.  🔍 CSC investigations FAQ   Key questionWhat CBS Sports learnedHow many programs are under investigation?Between five and 10 Power Four programs, including multiple CFP contenders.What is being investigated?Potential revenue-sharing cap evasion and NIL violations involving schools, athletes and third parties.How are investigations being conducted?Investigators have visited campuses and conducted in-person interviews.Have any investigations concluded?None of the longer-term investigations has been completed.What could complicate enforcement?Schools have not signed the participation agreement intended to strengthen the CSC's authority.Schools are allowed to spend around $21.5 million on their student athletes in the 2026-27 academic calendar year through a revenue sharing model approved in the historic NCAA v. House legal settlement.  
Any money a student-athlete receives from a third-party must clear the CSC approval process, where it's examined to see if the deal meets a fair-market range of compensation. In July, the CSC amended its rules to exempt all deals between $600 and $15,000 from the range of compensation review as long as that athlete has made $50,000 or less in "associated" deals. If the athlete is above that $50,000 number, the review is back in effect.  With seven college football rosters ballooning into the $40 million and, in a few cases, $50 million range, according to previous CBS Sports reporting, schools are spending well beyond the rev share number, which is meant to serve for all sports. Given $40 million football rosters and $10 million-plus basketball rosters just to be competitive, schools are attempting to generate tens of millions in third-party money for their athletes just to remain competitive. There is no cap on how much a team can spend as long as the deals are submitted and approved as being in accordance with the fair market range of compensation through the CSC's process.  In September, the CSC reported that through its platform NIL GO it had cleared $227.25 million in deals between July 1 and Aug. 31. However, it failed to clear $67.08 million during that period in deals that did not meet fair-market-value standards or the terms of the House Settlement agreement.  
Since NIL Go launched, it's cleared $582.5 million and denied $156.9 million in deals.  When millions get held up in the NIL Go system, some teams look for ways around the rules to deliver the payments they promised their athletes.  Sources have indicated the CSC isn't even holding up all the deals it could. Many submitted deals don't meet fair market value nor can it be proven the athlete ever provided the deliverables promised.  
"[The CSC] could discipline 100 student athletes tomorrow who have not fulfilled their NIL obligations," a source said. "The reality is, no one wanted them to. No one cared if they did. If they were real deals, the person would have made them do the obligations. The fact that they didn't do the obligations shows this was a sham deal from the start. Who's the person who put together that sham deal? It's not the student athlete."  The CSC has run into considerable hurdles in its investigations.  Its attempts to get all 68 Power Four institutions to sign a participation agreement have gone unfulfilled. The participation agreement was viewed as a critical piece of the House settlement, strengthening the CSC's ability to force schools to comply with investigations and potential penalties as well as require those institutions to waive the right to sue over any enforcement decision. It would have also prohibited schools from assisting in lawsuits i.e. a state attorney general suing on the school's behalf with its cooperation.  There was brief momentum behind getting the schools to sign the agreement but the CSC could never get all Power 4 conferences on board with it at the same time and has all but abandoned its hopes of it ever happening.  
Without the power of the participation agreement, the CSC has consistently faced the same problems the NCAA did whenever it tried to enforce its rules. Every school loves to say it wants the rules to be enforced but embodies a "rules for thee, but not for me" mentality. While there are exceptions, more often than not schools aggressively respond with outside counsel and a non-compliant attitude. Often it would take weeks, if not months, for schools to respond to CSC's requests for information.  "This is the hardest enforcement challenge in sports in the United States," one source told CBS Sports. "It's not even close in my mind." High-ranking staffers have long had a skeptical view on whether the CSC will actually be able to enforce its rules.  
With so many programs aggressively attempting to skirt around requirements built into the system, it's created an environment in which there's pressure on decision makers to break the rules to remain competitive.  "The problem with the CSC stuff is, what are they going to say: (This school) is ineligible?" a Power Four GM said. "They don't have teeth to enforce it. The big ones, we all knew that. We've talked about this pretty openly before.  "The GM position I truly believe you're going to get fired for performance or fired for cause. You just choose which one. And if you're fired for cause you chose to go down that road and it's a fine line to walk." 
To this point, previous reporting has unveiled CSC inquiries into schools such as LSU, Kansas and Nebraska. The inquiry into LSU was quickly resolved in February and did not involve the football program. The CSC won its first arbitration case after Nebraska challenged a decision to deny a collection of multi-million dollar deals involving 18 football players.  Those inquiries are separate from the multiple long-term investigations the CSC is currently conducting.   Documents obtained by CBS Sports through a public-records request to North Carolina show the school engaged in communication with the CSC over its dealings with a third-party NIL company. More than two-dozen UNC football and basketball staffers were asked about their communication with the entity. The school told the CSC that only basketball GM Jim Tanner and football GM Michael Lombardi had contact with the company. Lombardi told the CSC he used its software for "recruiting purposes." 
Lombardi resigned from the program on Sept. 3 amid an internal investigation into a human resources complaint against him.  Asked recently about the status of CSC investigations, ACC commissioner Jim Phillips said the CSC needs the authority to enforce the rules the membership agreed to. "It's gotten better," Phillips said. "I think with the footing of the CSC and the work that [President] Charlie Baker has done from an NCAA standpoint, there's been more synergy over this last year. And there needs to be because they have to work in unison. As I look towards the future, I only think that that's going to get stronger as we go forward, but when you don't have all of the tools necessary in enforcement, whether the NCAA or the CSC, it still leaves a hole in enforcement. You know, there's a lot of cases that are out there. We have some in our conference with student-athletes and tampering and the rest of it, but until you have the authority necessary to do some of these things, there's always going to be a little bit of a lag, but I feel good overall."

title: Bengals' Jordan Battle reveals subtle Malik Willis tell ahead of Week 5 matchup against Dolphins - CBS Sports
description: Cincinnati might have a leg up on Miami thanks to this scouting revelation
body:
Cincinnati might have a leg up on Miami thanks to this scouting revelation
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:13 pm ET

            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When the Cincinnati Bengals hit the road in Week 5 for their matchup against the Miami Dolphins, their defensive players will be on the lookout for a quirk in Malik Willis' passing mechanics. The Dolphins quarterback purportedly has a tell in his delivery that Cincinnati could use to time up its coverage.Bengals safety Jordan Battle detailed Willis' habit and what it means for the defensive backfield."He has a slight little tap before every throw, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball," Battle said after the Bengals' Thursday practice. "He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that gives the read to break."Revealing the tell before the game comes with its risks. If Willis and the Dolphins were not already keen on this tendency, they certainly are now. They may have already discovered it through self-scouting, however. And if not, three days may not be long enough to permanently eliminate the habit from Willis' mechanics.If the tell persists on Sunday and the Bengals' safeties come up with an interception, it may not be a coincidence.
The Bengals would gladly use any advantage they can find in pass defense, considering their struggles across the first four weeks of the season. They rank in the bottom half of the league in the following metrics.CategoryValueNFL RankEPA per pass-0.0317thInterceptions1T-25thTime to throw (sec.)2.9525thPass yards per game233.826thAvg. yards of separation3.827thOn paper, Willis presents a more manageable test for the Cincinnati defense than the quarterbacks they faced thus far: Trevor Lawrence, Aaron Rodgers, C.J. Stroud and Baker Mayfield. Willis' 712 passing yards are the fewest of any quarterback who has played four games. He also has the fourth-lowest passer rating among qualifiers.Still, as a mobile signal-caller, Willis offers challenges to a unit that has not found much success in containing the pass.
"He's obviously dangerous with his feet," Battle said. "We know we gotta be alert for that. Third-and-longs, they will run quarterback draws. In the passing game, he will extend plays, so we gotta be good downfield, DBs plastering. So we gotta be alert for that. He will take chances. We just gotta be alert on guys, where they're lined up."
